To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the butyrate-producing microbiota of ulcerative colitis is altered in comparison to healthy people, and the microbiome composition in ulcerative colitissufferers is different than in healthy people.
The results of the present study indicate that the microbiome in patients with active UC in North India differs significantly from that in healthy subjects.

the butyrate-producing bacterium, Roseburia intestinalis, was significantly increased in the feces of patients with active UC compared with healthy controls, while the other two butyrate-producing species, Eubacterium rectale and Faecalibacterium prausnitzii were decreased in patients with active UC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the bacterial species that are associated with the development of ulcerative colitis in patients in North India.
a better understanding of the mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of UC.
the study of bacterial populations in patients with ulcerative colitis and in normal controls in North India.

the use of a probiotic in the treatment of UC is not yet established.
the results of our study suggest that the use of probiotics is not associated with a significant reduction in the risk of CDI.
the use of probiotics in ulcerative colits is promising but the evidence is insufficient to support the clinical application in ulcerative colitus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gut microbiota is altered in patients with UC and this alteration is associated with the clinical phenotype.
the microbiome is a key player in the pathogenesis of UC, with the butyrate-producing bacterial group playing a significant role in the pathogenesis.
the gut microbiota in ulcerative colitic patients of north India has been found to be significantly different in comparison to that in the control group.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the microbiome is not a static entity and that there is a lot of variation in the composition of gut bacteria in the same individual over time.
the microbiota of ulcerative colitis (UC) patients is characterized by the absence of butyrate-producing bacterial groups.
we have identified a group of bacteria that are associated with a healthy gut and are not found in patients with IBD.
